decisions.statement: A subagent that exists is a page that exists.
A subagent its seat has seen return has no page.
A stop ends a turn rather than a subagent, so a stop alone takes no page.
A subagent the seat's transcript still names as one that has not returned keeps its page.
A subagent resuming takes up the page that subagent had.
The seat is named by the page the index has for the id the call runs under.
A payload naming no subagent leaves the subagent pages unchanged.
A start naming no kind puts up nothing.
This hook changes the subagent pages rather than judging a call.
The subagent begins and ends either way.
The seat's id reaches the take-down as the seat's id reaches the put-up.
A landing refused after this hook stepped aside leaves its reason in a log.
A page a refusal left unwritten is put up from that log.
The landing left to finish here and the restore of a dirty akasha take one lock.
A page half-landed by a process that died is swept by the next process to take that lock.

definition: a subagent's page, put up when it starts and taken away when it stops
